questions.question:
In the following question, a sentence is given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives choose the one which best expresses the sentence in Indirect/Direct Speech. 

The coach proposed that they should wait for the announcement of the results.

options.text: The Coach told them, "You wait. The results will be announced soon".
The Coach wanted the results to be announced so he said,"wait!".
"We shall wait for the announcement of the results", said the Coach.
"Wait for results announcement", the Coach said.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **"We shall wait for the announcement of the result", said the Coach.**

questions.question:
Change the following sentence to Direct Speech

Sunil Chhetri said that for the Indian team every match was war and every game a fight.

options.text: Sunil Chhetri said, "For the Indian team, every match is war and every game a fight."
Sunil Chhetri said "For Indians, every match was a fight and every game was a war,"
Sunil Chhetri said to the Indian team "You have to fight in each match like you are in a war and as if every game is a fight,"
Sunil Chhetri said, "Indian Team has to have to fight in each match to win the war"

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** **__***Sunil Chhetri said, "For the Indian team, every match is war and every game a fight."***__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• The given sentence is in Indirect Speech. As per the question, we have to change it into Direct Speech.
 
• The process of transformation is as follows:
 
 
• 'said' remain as it is.
 
• Comma and inverted commas will be inserted.
 
• The conjunction 'that' will be removed.
 
• Past indefinite tense changes to present indefinite tense
 
 
• ​'was' changes to 'is'. ​
 
 
 
 

**Hence, the correct answer will be: -***Sunil Chhetri said, "For the Indian team, every match is war and every game a fight."*

questions.question:
**Change the following sentence to Direct Speech.**

Mrs. Murthy asked the grief-stricken mother how the stove had burst.

options.text: Mrs.Murthy asked the grief-stricken mother,"How did the stove burst?"
Mrs.Murthy asked the grief-stricken mother, "How do the stove burst"?
Mrs.Murthy asked the grief-stricken mother,"Did you see how the stove burst?"
Mrs.Murthy asked the grief-stricken mother. "Why did the stove burst?"

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** option 1 i.e.** *'Mrs. Murthy asked the grief-stricken mother, "How did the stove burst?"'*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__***

__
 
• We need to change indirect speech into direct speech; for that reverse the rules of converting direct into indirect speech.
 
• According to rule, the assertive (positive) form after the reporting verb 'asked' should be changed into interrogative (question) form.
 
• If the sentence in indirect speech is in past perfect tense (had +V3) , it will change to past tense (Did + V1)
 
• **For example __**- He said that he had seen a clown*.* **(Indirect speech**) will be converted into He said*, "I saw a clown."*** (Direct speech).**

**​**

Hence, from the above explanation, the direct speech of the sentence will be - *Mrs Murthy asked the grief-stricken mother, "How did the stove burst?"'*

questions.question:
**Select the option that is the direct form of the given sentence.**

Brinda told her doctor that she was leaving for Boston the next day.

options.text: Brinda told to her doctor, “I will be leaving for Boston the next day”.
Brinda told her doctor, “I was leaving for Boston tomorrow”.
Brinda said to her doctor, “I am leaving for Boston tomorrow.”
Brinda had told her doctor, “She was leaving for Boston the next day”.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'​Brinda said to her doctor, “I am leaving for Boston tomorrow.”'**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• ** **The given sentence is in **indirect form.**
 
• To change it to direct form, we need to do the following - 
 
 
• Change in pronoun - In direct speech the pronoun changes to first person. So, **'she' will become 'I'.**
 
• Change in statement sentence - In direct speech, the 'told' is converted either to 'said' or remains the same. So, it either remains '**told' or becomes 'said'.**
 
• Change in tense - The **past continuous tense (was leaving) **in the indirect speech changes to **present continuous tense (am leaving)** in direct speech.
 
 
 
• Only **option 3** covers all three changes making it the correct answer.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate direct form of the given sentence.**

Anurag says that he would like to be an electronics engineer when he grows up.

options.text: Anurag said, “I will like to be an electronics engineer when I grow up.”
Anurag says, “He likes to be an electronics engineer when he grows up.”
Anurag says, “I like to be an electronics engineer when I grow up.”
Anurag says, “I would like to be an electronics engineer when I grow up.”

questions.solution:
The correct answer is- **Anurag says, “I would like to be an electronics engineer when I grow up.” **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Let's look at the steps to change the sentence from indirect to direct speech:
 
• When the **indirect **speech is in an assertive form, we follow the steps given below:
 
 
• The reporting verb says will remain the same as no object is mentioned after it.
 
• Connector 'that' is replaced by a comma and inverted commas.
 
• The personal pronouns will be changed according to the subject and object of the reporting verb.
 
• ​Here the 3rd person 'he' will change into the 1st person 'I' as per the object.
 
• The tense of indirect/reported speech will remain the same as the reporting verb(says) is in the present tense.
 
 
 
• ​At last line up the remaining part.

 
 
• 
 
Following these steps, we finally get- *Anurag says, “I would like to be an electronics engineer when I grow up.” *

questions.question:
**Directions: Select the most appropriate direct form of the given sentence.**

The salesman said that he had verified all the bills while the goods were being packed.

options.text: The salesman said, “I have verified all the bills while the goods are packed.”
The salesman said, “He had verified all the bills while the goods was being packed.”
The salesman said, “I am verifying all the bills while the goods are being packed.
The salesman said, “I verified all the bills while the goods were being packed.”

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **The salesman said, “I verified all the bills while the goods were being packed.”**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/64e177b3c5c5cb81c12b3d5b5ddabaaf474cdad3d6098992ca6592786c8147d6.png] 

__
 
• The **given sentence** is an **indirect speech.**
 
• The **basic rules** for changing or __**__converting indirect speech into direct speech__:**
 
 
• The **commas and inverted commas** are **added** and '**that**' is **removed**.
 
• The second person '**he**' will be changed into the first person **'I'**.
 
• The **past perfect tense** format '**Subject + had + V3 (verified) + Object'** will be changed into the **past simple tense** format '**Subject + V2 (verified) + Object'.**
 
 
 
• From the following rules, we get the correct sentence as **option 4*.***

questions.question:
**Directions: Select the most appropriate direct form of the given sentence.**

Anshul told me that his mother was not at home and that she would be back the following day.

options.text: Anshul said to me, “My mother is not at home. She will be back tomorrow.”
Anshul said to me, “My mother was not at home. She will be back the following day.”
Anshul said to me, “My mother is not at home. She would be back the following day.”

questions.solution:
